speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: asked	the Minister for Defence (a) whether he can provide an update on the seizure of Singapore's Terrex Infantry Carrier Vehicles in Hong Kong; (b) whether Singapore is likely to get the vehicles back; and (c) if not, whether there are any remedies available to us.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: asked	the Minister for Defence (a) whether he can provide an update on the seizure of Singapore's Terrex Infantry Carrier Vehicles in Hong Kong; and (b) whether there is a roadmap and timeline for exchanges with the Hong Kong authorities to secure their release.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Each year, SAF moves over 700 military platforms using commercial carriers to all parts of the world in Asia, Australia, Europe and the United States (US).

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The SAF's contracts with these shipping companies and agents require them to comply with established protocols and all relevant international and local port rules.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But the contracts leave it to the shipping companies to designate routes and ports, because this is their core business.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Neither the SAF, Singapore, nor indeed most other countries, operate on the assumption that our cargo will be arbitrarily seized when transiting reputable foreign ports.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: SAF has followed these procedures for shipping military equipment for over 30 years without any significant incidents.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Neither does the Republic of Singapore Navy (RSN) have transport ships with that scale and capability to ship all this equipment.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: However, our Landing Ship Tanks (LSTs), currently our largest multi-purpose and transport ships, are due for replacement.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We will consider if we need to replace them with ships of larger capacity.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: There are some exceptions, albeit rare, when SAF does not use commercial shipping companies, or will apply special considerations if we do, based on security risk assessments.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For example, as we did previously, when we shipped advanced weapon and sensor systems or submarines back to Singapore previously, the special measures include chartering whole ships, mandating direct shipments, deploying protection forces or even converting the commercial ship to a State Marine Ensign.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The Terrex troop carrier vehicles did not fall into this special category.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Members have asked if military secrets have been compromised due to the detention of the Terrexes.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: As MINDEF has stated, the detained Terrexes and other equipment were being used for training and do not contain any sensitive equipment.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Arising from this incident, SAF has reviewed its shipping procedures comprehensively to reduce the risk of SAF equipment being taken hostage en route.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Where we think the risk of detention of SAF assets has gone up, whether in Asia or any other part of the world, we will impose extra precautions even if this means incurring higher freight charges.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Alternatively, SAF may consider housing that equipment at overseas training sites to avoid shipping them altogether, and procure additional units to meet operational requirements, where necessary.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: In the present case, the SAF Terrexes were transiting in Hong Kong, one of the world's busiest and most established transhipment points.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: They were in transit on board the ship when they were ordered to be off-loaded by the Hong Kong authorities and detained.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: They are protected by sovereign immunity, even though they were being shipped by commercial carriers.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: This means that they are immune from any measures of constraint abroad.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: They cannot legally be detained or confiscated by other countries.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: This principle is well-established under international law, and we are advised by lawyers that it is also the law in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR).

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Accordingly, the Singapore Government has asserted our sovereign rights over the SAF Terrexes.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We have informed the Hong Kong Government on several occasions over the last two months, both through lawyers and our Consul-General in Hong Kong, that the detained Terrexes and other equipment belong to the Government of Singapore and are, therefore, immune from any measures of constraint.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Prime Minister Lee has also written to Chief Executive CY Leung of Hong Kong on this matter to reiterate the same message.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The Hong Kong authorities have responded that the investigation is ongoing and will take some time to complete and that the Hong Kong government will handle the matter in accordance with their laws.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Adherence to the rule of law has been the fundamental basis for peace and stability in the last half century in Asia.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It has enabled countries both large and small to build trust and confidence in one another, cooperate and prosper together.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: These are the very principles incorporated in the Treaty of Amity and Co-operation whose signatories pledge "to promote regional peace and stability through abiding respect for justice and the rule of law".

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Whether APL, the shipping company in this case, has complied with the rules of Hong Kong port is a matter between APL and the Hong Kong authorities, which should follow the due process of Hong Kong law.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: That issue between APL and Hong Kong Customs affects neither the legal position of the Terrexes nor the Singapore Government's rights.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We, therefore, look forward to the Hong Kong government returning our Terrexes in accordance with international law.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Singapore and Hong Kong have long enjoyed good and friendly relations.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We hope the matter will be resolved satisfactorily and our friendly relations will endure.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Is Singapore also considering commercial claims against the carrier, in the event of any delay or losses that may arise if the Terrexes are not returned or if there are some other delays in the return?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: In addition, all SAF cargo we ship is insured against losses under some conditions.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We have to check if the insurance claims are applicable for this particular incident.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Thirdly, what would be the loss of potential future earnings for Singapore in this piece of defence technology which even the US is interested in?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Not only in the future of losing our equipment, but that has been our prevailing policy.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: That is why we have, as I said, for that special category, imposed special conditions on ourselves and our commercial shippers and whether it is in the form of port-to-port or converting commercial ships to State Marine Ensign when we brought back our submarines.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But in this particular instance, the Terrexes do not fall into that special category, and we leave it to the carriers to designate the ports.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Hong Kong is an international port of repute, and there is no reason to believe that our SAF assets will be seized.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I have related to Members what the Hong Kong government had responded with.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: That is, at complete face value, what has happened.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: They have said that they need time and that they will handle it in accordance with Hong Kong's laws, and we welcome that assurance.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: ST Kinetics or ST Engineering will have to do its work.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But whether this increases the notoriety of the platform and, therefore, increases its selling potential or not, who is to say?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It is theoretical and I want to defer from answering that question.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: One, does MINDEF consider the details of the Terrexes' armour or any other technical specifications to be classified information?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Second, does the confiscated shipment include any equipment or technology that falls under some export control regime or restrictions to China?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The easiest way to answer Mr Singh's question is that you can purchase the Terrexes and associated equipment on the open market.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, they do not contain any sensitive equipment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As the Minister has mentioned, the detention of our Terrexes appears to be contrary to Hong Kong and international law.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It could be a helpful barometer for how businesses assess Hong Kong's reputation as an international port.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The Hong Kong government has responded on the various occasions that we had asserted our sovereign immunity as well as asked for updates that their investigations are ongoing.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: As I had said in my reply, they have said that they will settle this in accordance with Hong Kong law.
